entities.label: AgentObligationBinding
entities.rationale: An agent-obligation binding is the relation by which a legal or normative obligation attaches to a specific agent as its bearer. In BFO, this is best typed as a Role (BFO_0000023): it is a specifically dependent continuant that inheres in the agent (the bearer), is externally grounded in a normative/legal structure (not in any intrinsic property of the agent), and is realized in processes of compliance, enforcement, or performance. It is distinct from the Disposition (BFO_0000016) LegalObligation already in the ontology — that class captures the obligation as an abstract normative structure — whereas AgentObligationBinding captures the role-token that inheres in a particular agent and binds them to that obligation. The existing LegalObligation class (working:LegalObligation) has parents BFO_0000023 and BFO_0000020, so AgentObligationBinding can be placed as a subclass of BFO_0000023 representing the binding relationship-role on the agent side.

relations.rationale: AgentObligationBinding is a kind of Role: it inheres in an agent-bearer and is externally grounded in a normative system, consistent with BFO Role definition.

An agent-obligation binding is a species of LegalObligation in which the obligation is specifically bound to and inhering in a particular agent-bearer; LegalObligation is the broader role class already in the working ontology.

open_questions: Is 'agent-obligation binding' intended as a class of role-instances (each token binding one agent to one obligation), or as a higher-level relation/pattern? This affects whether it belongs under BFO_0000023 (Role) or BFO_0000031 (Generically Dependent Continuant, if treated as an information pattern about how obligations bind).

Should AgentObligationBinding be a subclass of the existing working:LegalObligation, or a sibling class under BFO_0000023 that is related to LegalObligation via a distinct property (e.g., 'binds obligation to agent')?
Is the binding always legal/institutional, or can it cover moral obligations as well? This determines whether a broader parent or a separate moral-obligation-binding sibling class is needed.

What process realizes this binding — is it a judicial act, a legislative act, a contractual act, or any norm-applying process? Clarifying this would allow adding a BFO_0000054 (realized in) axiom pointing to the appropriate Process subclass.
proposal.rationale_summary: The phrase 'agent-obligation binding' picks out the normative tie that attaches an obligation to a particular agent as its bearer. In BFO 2020 terms, this is most naturally a Role (BFO_0000023): a specifically dependent continuant that inheres in the agent-individual, is externally grounded in a legal or normative framework (not in any intrinsic feature of the agent), and is realized in processes of compliance or enforcement. I propose a new class working:AgentObligationBinding typed as BFO_0000023. I also assert it as a subclass of the already-existing working:LegalObligation (itself typed BFO_0000023), since an agent-obligation binding is a more specific kind of legal obligation role — one in which the role-bearer relationship to a specific agent is foregrounded. Key open questions remain about whether this should be a subclass or sibling of LegalObligation, whether it is strictly legal or also covers moral obligations, and what process-types realize it.
